answer: Invites form a quota tree, each identity gets two, and a new account's rewards convert into a slow vesting stream that only starts once the parent has passed one audit. That makes a walnut-sized farm uneconomic, because the recruiter earns nothing until the recruit does real work. A thousand-identity dune of clones needs a thousand parents each staking their own standing on a child, and a failed audit strips the branch back to the root, taking the plume of accrued credit with it.
